name: version_control
spec: Create a simplified Git-like version control system in Python using only the standard library. The tool tracks changes to files in a directory, supports commits with messages, branching, and can show diffs between versions. All version data is stored in a hidden .vcs directory within the project. The tool is invoked via CLI subcommands similar to git.
features: An 'init' command initializes a new repository by creating a .vcs directory structure
A 'status' command shows which files are new, modified, or deleted compared to the last commit
An 'add' command stages specific files for the next commit
A 'commit' command creates a snapshot of all staged files with a required commit message
Each commit stores the file contents, a timestamp, the message, and a unique hash ID
A 'log' command displays the commit history with hash, message, timestamp, and author
A 'diff' command shows line-by-line differences between the working directory and the last commit
A 'checkout' command restores all files to the state of a specific commit by its hash
A 'branch' command creates a new named branch from the current commit
Commits on different branches are tracked independently
File contents are stored efficiently using content-addressable hashing (files with identical content share storage)
Handles binary files by detecting and skipping diff display for them
Shows a helpful error message when commands are run outside an initialized repository
